The stem every file a design writes is named after

Source: R/design.R
design_stem.Rd

The slug of the design's name and language, which keeps letters and digits only. Two designs whose names differ only outside ASCII (two Chinese names, both with the language chinese) would share a slug and overwrite each other's files, and an all-Chinese name and language would give no slug at all. Whenever the name or the language holds a non-ASCII character, the stem therefore gains _ and the first eight hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the NFC-normalised UTF-8 text name|language. An empty slug is replaced by those eight digits. NFC keeps a precomposed and a decomposed accented letter on one stem. A design whose name and language hold no letter or digit at all is refused. Mirrors design_stem() in the Python package.

Usage

design_stem(design)

Arguments

design

A parsed design configuration.

Value

The file stem, such as "en_lexdec_english" or "chinese_14aadfa7".

Examples

design_stem(list(name = "en_lexdec", language = "english"))
#> [1] "en_lexdec_english"
# Two Chinese characters, written as code points to keep this file ASCII.
design_stem(list(name = intToUtf8(c(0x8bcd, 0x9891)), language = "chinese"))
#> [1] "chinese_14aadfa7"
